title: Servepath Constellation: percentile-c exploration dashboard for routes & models (streaming vs blocking)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: build a multi-panel exploratory dashboard (Servepath Constellation) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency across model routes with an explicit split for streaming vs non-streaming I/O, plus trace-links and error overlays. This ticket covers end-to-end work: metric tagging, pipeline aggregation changes, dashboard panels, SLO/alert updates, and rollout. Motivation: product teams and platform SREs need a single, query-performant surface to quickly triage route-specific tail latency regressions and confirm whether regressions are correlated with streaming I/O, model variants, or request shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes per-route and per-model p50/p95/p99 with toggle for streaming vs blocking and a combined view
Percentiles are calculated from HDR histograms at ingestion or via pre-aggregated summary buckets to keep dashboard queries < 3s for 30-day windows
Each latency datapoint includes trace link (trace_id) and request metadata: route, model, io_mode, request_shape, commit_version
Error-rate overlay panel (5xx/4xx) correlated by same cohort selections
Can filter down to customer cohorts and conversation/request id to attach traces
Telemetry and metrics changes are backward-compatible for existing dashboards and instrumented clients
Rollout completed to hosted region us-west-2 with no customer-facing regressions and dashboards added to Console -> Performance -> Servepath Constellation
technical_notes: Metrics: add metric tags: route, model_name, io_mode=streaming|blocking, request_shape_bucket, conversation_id (optional). Use existing route slug convention to avoid new cardinality explosion.
Histogram strategy: ingest HDR histograms at 1s resolution and compute percentiles in the TSDB (preferred) OR store precomputed p50/p95/p99 in a rollup table if query latency becomes an issue.

Tracing hooks: emit trace_id in metrics envelope for top N slow requests to allow index-join in the UI and linking to Trace UI. Add sampling rule for slow-path (p95+) to increase trace retention temporarily.

Pipeline changes: update metrics pipeline to carry new tags through Prometheus -> remote write -> Clickhouse/TSDB and validate cardinality. Introduce a compressing aggregator for request_shape_bucket.
Query design: use a heatmap panel for percentile surface, a sparklines panel for per-model trends, and a cohort selector (route + model + io_mode). Provide a compare mode for streaming vs blocking.
SLO/alerting: introduce an SLI for route-specific p99 exceeding baseline for >10m and an automatic incident stub linking to dashboard + recent traces.
Perf considerations: ensure dashboard queries use pre-aggregated indexes; fallback to sampled cohort query if full query too heavy. Add caching with 30s TTL for heavy cohorts.
Data retention: keep raw histograms for 14 days, roll up percentiles for 90 days. This matches other latency dashboards.
Backward compatibility: metrics with missing io_mode default to 'blocking' for now and instrumentations will be rolled out gradually across runtimes.
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement metric tagging in runtime (serving agents) behind feature flag and emit HDR histogram; deploy canary to internal traffic
Week 2: update metrics pipeline to pass tags and store histograms; create pre-aggregated percentile store and validate values against raw traces
Week 3: dashboard build in Console (dev environment) + design review; wire trace-links and cohort selectors
Week 4: soft launch in us-west-2 for a subset of customers and internal teams; monitor query latency and cardinality
Week 5: full region rollout, update SLOs/alerts, and announce in #observability and release notes
